title: An AI security agent found a one-click Granola account takeover, now patched
friendlyTitle: Granola fixed a serious link security problem
summary: Strix reports that its autonomous security system found a chain in Granola’s Electron desktop app that could let a malicious notification link inherit a privileged application bridge and take over an account. Granola shipped server-side and follow-up fixes in June, and both companies report no evidence of exploitation.
friendlySummary: Strix’s AI security agents found that one bad link could have taken over a Granola account through its desktop app. Granola fixed the issue and found no sign that attackers used it.
whyItMatters: Desktop AI apps often combine web content with access to local files, sessions and device features, making navigation boundaries especially important. The disclosure offers a concrete checklist: block untrusted navigation, narrow IPC interfaces and keep encryption keys outside the renderer.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI desktop apps can reach sensitive local information. App makers should strictly limit which web pages and commands receive that access.
